title: Daily withdrawal limit bypass (phantom)
root_cause: withdraw() does check-then-insert without any lock: it reads SUM(amount) for today and, if under DAILY_LIMIT, inserts. Under READ COMMITTED two concurrent transactions both read the same stale sum, both pass the check, and both insert, so the day total exceeds DAILY_LIMIT (lost-update / phantom race).
fix: Serialize withdrawals per account with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the accounts row at the start of the transaction, making the SUM check + INSERT + balance update atomic per account while leaving different accounts fully parallel.

repro_report.example_violation: account 1 withdrew 6000 today, above the daily limit of 5000

checks.name: same_behaviour
checks.detail: 40 sequential requests matched the original exactly

checks.name: agent_reproduction_test
checks.detail: the agent's own reproduction test passed 3/3 runs

fix_code:
"""ATM / UPI withdrawals with a per-account daily limit.

Each account may withdraw at most DAILY_LIMIT paise per calendar day.
"""
import psycopg

DAILY_LIMIT = 5_000  # ₹50 per day

MIGRATIONS: list[str] = []


class DailyLimitExceeded(Exception):
    pass


def withdraw(conn: psycopg.Connection, account_id: int, amount: int) -> None:
    with conn.transaction():
        # Serialize concurrent withdrawals for the same account so the
        # check-then-insert below is atomic: lock the account row first.
        # Different accounts lock different rows and proceed in parallel.
        # For an unknown account no row is locked and execution falls
        # through to the original statements below, preserving the
        # original error behaviour exactly.
        conn.execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM accounts WHERE id = %s FOR UPDATE",
            (account_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        (used,) = conn.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM withdrawals WHERE account_id = %s AND day = current_date",
            (account_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if used + amount > DAILY_LIMIT:
            raise DailyLimitExceeded(account_id)
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO withdrawals (account_id, amount) VALUES (%s, %s)", (account_id, amount))
        updated = conn.execute(
            "UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - %s WHERE id = %s RETURNING id", (amount, account_id)
        ).fetchone()
        if updated is None:
            raise ValueError("unknown account")
